findings.where: Article specimen: the three-item list under 'So, what are the key chapter topics?' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The list items have almost no line spacing, while the paragraphs just above have generous spacing. A wrapped item runs into the next one, and on phone four wrapped lines pile up like a block of fine print. The reading rhythm breaks at the first list, which is exactly what the brief asked this specimen to prove it can handle.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, who will add lists to Mark's articles, and the founder, who asked for type on a rhythm that holds when a list is added. A development-bank reader also finds the list harder to read than the text around it.

findings.where: Article specimen: the article title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law' against the subhead 'So, what are the key chapter topics?' (worst on phone)
findings.fault: The subhead is set as large as the article title, and on phone it is clearly larger, at the same heavy weight. A section inside the article outranks the article's own name, so the page seems to start again partway down.
findings.who_objects: A reader of Mark's article, who uses the heading sizes to tell the article's title from its sections and here gets the order the wrong way round.

findings.where: Article specimen: the image caption, then 'So, what are the key chapter topics?' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The subhead sits straight under the photo caption with no space before it. The caption looks like the subhead's kicker, and the new section does not read as starting. Elsewhere a subhead has room above it, so the spacing depends on what comes before it, which is the hand-tuned spacing the brief rules out.
findings.who_objects: The founder and Angélique, because the brief asks that adding an image and caption leave the rhythm intact. A reader, because the caption and the next section run together.

findings.where: First screen: the ghosted giant 'PPP' letters behind Mark's line (desktop behind the first two lines, phone at the right edge)
findings.fault: A second display word in pale blue sits behind the one large serif line and cuts through 'In my view, we are at / a turning point'. Its letter shapes compete with the heading's, so the one line the brief asks to stand alone has a shadow word under it, and 'PPP' reads as a typographic decoration.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brief asks for one very large serif line and scale contrast, not more elements. A visiting bank officer reading the first line, who has to read it through the letters behind it.

findings.where: Article specimen: the article title's apostrophe in 'World's', against the curly quotes in the subhead and body
findings.fault: The title's apostrophe is a straight typewriter mark with a gap after it, while the subhead and body use curly quotes. Like marks are set unlike, in the largest type on the article page.
findings.who_objects: A careful reader of a legal adviser's writing, who notices the typewriter mark in a headline that is otherwise well set.
